title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: To understand UnitedHealth Group, you must follow both the premium dollar and the claim dollar—because the same enterprise often sits on both sides of the ledger.
epigraph.author: Healthcare Systems Architecture Note

web_blocks.html: UnitedHealth Group operates through two complementary reporting platforms [5, 7]. UnitedHealthcare handles health benefits and insurance, serving 48.3 million medical consumers as of Q3 2026 [5, 7]. Optum delivers health services, pharmacy care, and healthcare technology, supporting over 120 million consumers [5, 7]. Optum sells clinical care, pharmacy fulfillment, and software directly to UnitedHealthcare. Because of that internal trade, consolidated reporting includes massive intersegment eliminations of $168.0 billion in FY2025 and $118.5 billion in 9M 2026 [5, 7]. Analyzing UNH cleanly requires examining each of the six underlying operating businesses separately.

web_blocks.caption: UNH Segment Revenues, Operating Earnings & Margins (Audited FY2024–FY2025 & 9M 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Effective Jan 1, 2026, UNH moved Optum Financial (including Optum Bank) from Optum Health to Optum Insight, recasting 9M 2026 results [5, 7]. In FY2025, Optum Rx generated 38% of consolidated EBIT while Optum Health posted a $(278)M operating loss. By 9M 2026, both UHC (4.8%) and Optum Health (4.3%) staged sharp margin recoveries.

web_blocks.title: UnitedHealthcare: Three Insurance Pillars & Real-World Examples

web_blocks.html: 1. UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual ($60.3B 9M 2026 rev; 29.8M commercial members): This unit serves large national employers, small businesses, and individuals on ACA exchanges [7]. Roughly 75% of commercial members (22.2 million) sit on fee-based Administrative Services Only (ASO) contracts [7]. Under ASO, the employer self-funds medical claims and pays UNH a predictable per-employee-per-month administrative fee, while 7.6 million members remain risk-based [7]. Concrete Example: A Fortune 500 manufacturer with 40,000 employees hires UHC on an ASO contract. Employees use UHC's national PPO network and digital portal while UHC adjudicates claims and negotiates hospital discounts. The employer reimburses claims weekly and pays UHC a fixed administrative fee plus stop-loss insurance.

2. UnitedHealthcare Medicare & Retirement ($126.9B 9M 2026 rev; 7.61M MA, 4.25M Medigap, 2.69M Part D members): This is the nation's largest Medicare Advantage (MA) insurer [5, 7]. It receives capitated monthly payments from CMS adjusted for member health risk (HCC scores) and Star Ratings [5, 7]. Concrete Example: A 72-year-old retired teacher in Phoenix with Type 2 diabetes enrolls in a $0-premium UHC Medicare Advantage PPO plan. CMS pays UHC a monthly risk-adjusted capitation rate, and UHC coordinates her primary care, drugs, and dental/vision benefits. An Optum HouseCalls nurse also conducts an annual in-home assessment to document chronic conditions and close preventive care gaps.

3. UnitedHealthcare Community & State ($71.4B 9M 2026 rev; 6.70M Medicaid members): This segment contracts with state governments to manage Medicaid, CHIP, and dual-eligible (Medicare plus Medicaid) populations [7]. Concrete Example: A state Medicaid agency hires UHC to manage care for 350,000 low-income families and complex behavioral-health beneficiaries. UHC receives a state-determined capitated rate per member per month. It then deploys community health workers and behavioral coaching to reduce avoidable emergency-room visits.

web_blocks.title: Optum: Three Health-Services Engines & Real-World Examples

web_blocks.html: 4. Optum Health ($102.0B FY25 rev; $70.5B 9M 2026 rev; 92M consumers served): Optum Health operates local physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, behavioral clinics, and home-health networks including LHC Group and Amedisys [5, 7, 9]. It takes full or partial capitated risk for roughly 4.3–5.0 million value-based care patients [5, 7, 9]. Concrete Example: An 80-year-old heart-failure patient leaves the hospital and is assigned to an Optum Care physician group and an Amedisys/LHC nurse. Instead of billing Medicare fee-for-service per visit, Optum Health receives a fixed share of the Medicare premium from UHC or another MA plan. It keeps the savings if home monitoring prevents a $25,000 hospital readmission.

5. Optum Insight ($19.4B FY25 rev; $16.0B 9M 2026 rev; 22.6% 9M26 margin): This is UNH's highest-margin technology, revenue-cycle, data-analytics, and (as of 2026) Optum Financial/Bank division [5, 7]. Key assets include Change Healthcare's clearinghouse, AI-enabled autonomous coding, digital prior-authorization tools, and Alegeus (acquired July 2026 for HSA/FSA accounts) [7, 9]. Concrete Example: A 12-hospital regional health system outsources its revenue-cycle management and claims scrubbing to Optum Insight. The hospital pays recurring multi-year fees out of a $32+ billion backlog to speed up insurer reimbursements and cut coding denials.

6. Optum Rx ($154.7B FY25 rev; $114.0B 9M 2026 rev; ~1.6B annual adjusted scripts): Optum Rx is one of the Big Three U.S. PBMs alongside CVS Caremark and Express Scripts [5, 7, 20]. It manages retail pharmacy networks, mail-order pharmacies, specialty/infusion pharmacies, and manufacturer rebate negotiations [5, 7, 20]. Concrete Example: A state-university employee with rheumatoid arthritis fills a biologic prescription through Optum Rx's specialty pharmacy. Optum Rx verifies prior authorization, ships temperature-controlled medication to her home, and coordinates nurse adherence calls. Under its 2026–2028 transparent fee model, it passes 100% of manufacturer rebates back to the university plan while charging a flat administrative fee [7].

web_blocks.title: Customer Concentration & Captive Intersegment Dependence
paragraphs: Single-Payer Sovereign Concentration: Per UNH's FY2025 Form 10-K, premium revenues from CMS rose to 44% of total consolidated revenues in FY2025 (up from 40% in both FY2024 and FY2023), making federal Medicare funding policy UNH's largest single counterparty risk [2, 29]. State Medicaid contracts and federal Part D/ACA programs add further government-tender concentration.

Captive Intersegment Funnel: In 9M 2026, affiliated UnitedHealthcare customers generated $118.46 billion (60.3%) of Optum's $196.30 billion gross revenue, including $68.91 billion (60.5%) of Optum Rx's $113.96 billion revenue and $43.53 billion (61.8%) of Optum Health's $70.49 billion revenue [29]. Consequently, when UHC intentionally contracted medical membership by 1.83 million lives YoY through Q3 2026 (to 48.30 million), Optum Rx's Q3 2026 adjusted scripts dropped 5.1% YoY (393 million vs 414 million) [7, 29]. On the provider-network side, UHC's November 18, 2026 CPESN USA partnership broadens Medicaid care delivery across independent community pharmacies in seven states [31].

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand why UnitedHealth Group is both admired by industrialists and investigated by antitrust regulators, look at one accounting line: $167.956 billion in corporate eliminations in 2025. That figure represents business that UnitedHealthcare—the nation's largest health insurer—sent internally to Optum, its sister services conglomerate. When you and I dissect UNH, we are not looking at a single company. We are looking at a sovereign-scale healthcare ecosystem where six businesses pass patients, prescriptions, and data across internal transfer-pricing bridges.

Let's walk through the insurance side first, because UnitedHealthcare is still the front door for 48.3 million Americans and $344.9 billion in annual revenue. Inside UnitedHealthcare, you have three very different economic engines. Employer & Individual is the steadier commercial backbone, where nearly three-quarters of its 29.8 million members sit on fee-based administrative contracts. Under those deals, large employers—say, a national automaker or a retail chain—bear the medical risk themselves and pay UHC a predictable fee to rent its network and process claims. Medicare & Retirement, by contrast, is a $170 billion-plus government risk business serving seniors. CMS pays UHC a fixed monthly check for each of its 7.6 million Medicare Advantage members, and profit depends on pricing utilization and risk-adjustment rules accurately. Community & State does the same for 6.7 million Medicaid and complex-needs beneficiaries on behalf of state governments.

Now step across the bridge into Optum, which generated $270.6 billion in 2025 revenue before eliminations. Optum Health is the clinical arm, spanning over 100,000 employed and affiliated physicians, surgery centers, behavioral clinics, and home-health nurses from LHC Group and Amedisys. When an elderly heart-failure patient leaves the hospital, Optum Health's value-based care model puts a nurse in her living room so she stays out of the emergency room. When that works, it saves the system money and earns Optum Health a healthy margin. Yet when Optum Health takes capitated risk contracts with third-party insurers whose rates lag rising acuity—as happened in 2025—it can swing from $7.8 billion in operating profit to a $278 million loss in a single year.

Optum Insight is the exact opposite. It is a capital-light, high-margin software, analytics, and financial-infrastructure business sitting inside hospital billing departments and health-plan back offices. In January 2026, UNH moved Optum Bank and Optum Financial into Optum Insight, helping operating margins expand to 22.6% in the first nine months of 2026. Think of Optum Insight as the plumbing and AI-powered billing brain of American healthcare. It scrubs claims, automates prior authorizations, and manages health savings accounts.

Finally, Optum Rx is the $155 billion pharmacy engine, processing roughly 1.6 billion adjusted prescriptions a year across retail networks, home delivery, and specialty pharmacies. Historically, PBMs made money in ways that drew fierce Congressional and FTC criticism. They retained portions of manufacturer rebates or profited from spread pricing between what a plan paid and what a pharmacy received. In 2026, facing FTC settlements and legislative pressure, Optum Rx is pivoting toward a transparent, flat per-member fee model with 100% rebate pass-through by 2028. For you and me, the takeaway is clear: UNH's six businesses form a self-reinforcing flywheel when underwriting is disciplined, but captive synergy also concentrates regulatory and execution risk.

Take a moment to trace how these six pieces interact on a single patient's journey, because that is where UNH's structural advantage—and regulatory exposure—lives. Imagine a 74-year-old retiree in Florida enrolled in a UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plan. She picks up her blood-pressure and diabetes drugs through Optum Rx's home-delivery pharmacy. She sees a primary-care doctor employed by Optum Health who uses Optum Insight's clinical-decision software at the point of care. If she needs knee surgery, her claim clears through Change Healthcare's electronic network. Three different UNH subsidiaries touch that single patient's care pathway. They capture administrative fees, value-based savings, and specialty-pharmacy volume that a standalone insurer would pay to outside vendors. When every node is priced accurately, UNH earns a stacked margin across the healthcare dollar. When CMS cuts benchmarks or utilization spikes, UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health feel the pain together. Understanding that internal linkage is essential before you evaluate UNH's long-term earnings power.

Before leaving UNH's business architecture, underline one concentration fact disclosed in the audited FY2025 Form 10-K that casual readers often miss: premium revenues from CMS alone reached 44% of UNH's entire consolidated revenue in 2025, up from 40% in 2023 and 2024. That means nearly half of UNH's top line depends directly on federal Medicare rate-setting, Star Ratings, and risk-adjustment formulas. Inside Optum, meanwhile, more than 60% of 9M 2026 segment revenue—$118.5 billion out of $196.3 billion, including $68.9 billion at Optum Rx and $43.5 billion at Optum Health—came from affiliated UnitedHealthcare members. When UHC shrinks membership by nearly two million lives to protect underwriting margins, Optum's script and clinic volumes feel the downstream contraction immediately.

book_callouts.title: Follow the Risk-Bearing vs. Fee-Based Split
book_callouts.text: Not all UNH revenue carries the same economic risk. Distinguish between capitated risk revenue (where UNH eats medical inflation) and fee-based/software revenue (where UNH earns predictable spreads).
bullets: Risk-bearing: Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Commercial Risk-Based, and Optum Health full-risk value-based care.
Fee-based / Asset-light: Commercial ASO (22.2M lives), Optum Insight software & Optum Bank, and Optum Rx administrative/specialty dispensing fees.
